critical_code_review_comments: master_import.py _is_example_row is only evaluated for rn == 2; if the user inserts a row above the contoh row (or leaves it lower down) the sample row will be imported as real data. Consider checking the example signature for any row, not only row 2.

routers/data_management.py import_commit does not validate the `sheets` form field against SHEETS keys: a typo (e.g. sheets=custommers) silently commits nothing while still creating a pre_import snapshot and an import_logs entry with an empty summary. Return 400 for unknown keys and/or skip the snapshot when no sheet will be processed.

services/master_import.py _existing_index loads every non-deleted document of the target collection into a Python dict for each sheet (3 keys per customer). For a real migration with tens of thousands of customers this is a large memory spike; consider projecting only the match fields (name/phone/email/plate).

commit() writes documents one-by-one with await per row and re-reads db.vehicles.distinct('code') inside the loop for every new vehicle without a code — O(n) extra round-trips. Compute the code counter once before the loop and use bulk_write for inserts.

commit() has no transaction/rollback: a failure halfway (e.g. Mongo error on sheet 5) leaves earlier sheets written and no import log; the pre_import snapshot is the only recovery path. Worth logging partial progress before re-raising.
